title: What a Missouri CDS Caregiver Can and Can't Do (Rules That Protect Your Pay)
short_title: What a CDS caregiver can and can't do
description: Hired as a CDS caregiver in Missouri? Here's what you may and may not do on the job: the plan of care, helping only the person named on it, what to do when you're asked for more, supplies, the monthly limit on hours, no work before screening, and respecting their home.

parts.head: What a CDS caregiver can and can't do
parts.sub: Rules that protect you, and your paycheck
parts.text: You've been hired as a CDS caregiver. So what can you do on the job, and what can't you? I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS. These rules protect you, the person you care for, and your paycheck.

parts.head: It's the whole list
parts.sub: The approved tasks, how often, and the monthly limit
parts.text: It all starts with the plan of care, from the state assessment. It lists the tasks the person is approved for, how often, and the most care they can have each month. Ask to see it, and ask them to walk you through how they want each task done.

parts.head: Do the tasks on the plan
parts.sub: Their way, actively working the whole time
parts.text: You may do the tasks on the plan of care, the way the person you care for teaches you. You're actively working the whole time you're clocked in, and you can ask questions any time you're unsure.

parts.head: Tasks off the plan
parts.sub: Unauthorized medication tasks. Idle time or errands on the clock.
parts.text: You may not do tasks that aren't on the plan, do medication tasks that aren't authorized, or sit idle and run personal errands while you're clocked in.

parts.head: Help anyone else in the house
parts.sub: Not the spouse, grandkids, visitors or pets
parts.text: And here's the one that trips up good caregivers. You help only the person named on the plan of care. Not their spouse, not their grandkids, not visitors, and not their pets. It can feel unkind to say no. Say it anyway, kindly.

parts.head: Stop, ask, and call us
parts.sub: Even if they say it's OK
parts.text: If you're asked to do something that isn't on the plan, stop, ask, and call us. Even if the person says it's okay, and even though they're the employer, it can't be done or recorded. Asking first is always easier than fixing it later.

parts.head: Supplies aren't yours to buy
parts.sub: Cleaning supplies, gloves, gas, a vehicle
parts.text: You don't have to buy supplies. Cleaning supplies, gloves, gas, and a vehicle are the consumer's responsibility. If something's missing, tell them, and tell us if it doesn't get fixed.

parts.head: Hours have a hard limit
parts.sub: Hours past the approved amount can't be paid
parts.text: The state approves a set amount of care each month. We can only pay for what was approved, so hours worked past the limit can't be paid. Know your schedule, and speak up.

parts.head: No work before you're cleared
parts.text: And no work before your screening and paperwork are done. If someone asks you to start early, just to help out, the answer is no. That time can't be paid.

parts.head: It's their home
parts.sub: Knock. Ask first. Keep it private. No photos.
parts.text: You're in someone's home, helping with the most private parts of their life. Knock. Ask before moving their things. Keep their health and finances private, and never post photos of them or their home.

parts.head: Not sure? Call us.
parts.sub: Review it any time in the free Attendant Orientation
parts.text: When you're not sure, call us. That's what we're here for. You can also review all of this any time in the free Attendant Orientation online.
Questions? Call us at 417-218-2888, Monday to Friday, nine to four, or visit caringcds.com. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS. Thanks for watching.
